adjudications.reason: The quotation is in the record, spoken by Yoram Aridor presenting the bill on behalf of the Constitution, Law and Justice Committee, not by the Justice Minister as Coder A wrote; the record's footnote places the first-reading debate in Divrei HaKnesset, second session, booklet 38, p. 4002, and Aridor describes a lengthy sub-committee deliberation with no shortened procedure. First reading: exact date not stated, about eighteen months before the final vote of 31 March 1976, roughly 540 days, far outside thirty days. The record supports No rather than a blank because the definition's test is the thirty-day threshold, which the record's own statement settles.

adjudications.support: בסוף סעיף קטן (ב)(1) יבוא "אך לא יאוחר מששים ימים לפני תחילת שנת הכספים"
adjudications.reason: Value engaged: separation of powers only, as the principal subject; both coders concede the text touches it, and the definition reserves None for a text that engages none of the five values, with no weight threshold. Section 2 writes into the Basic Law a minimum of sixty days between the government's tabling of the budget bill and the fiscal year, securing the Knesset's time to exercise its power over public finance; section 1 only removes a duplicated approval requirement for tax regulations and is neutral. Nothing contradicts a value, so I adopt Coder A's reading.

adjudications.reason: The record Coder A cites holds: the sitting is the 266th of the 12th Knesset, Tuesday 28 Shevat 5751 (12 February 1991), and the third reading (electronic vote no. 16) carried 82 to 2 with 2 abstaining, figures the chair then repeated. The encyclopedia's table gives the coalition 66 MKs from Moledet's entry on 5 February 1991 until Tzomet left on 31 December 1991 (Likud 35, Shas 5, NRP 5, Movement for the Zionist Idea 5, Agudat Yisrael 4, Tehiya 3, Tzomet 2, Moledet 2, Degel HaTorah 2, Gur 1, Geulat Yisrael 1, Moria 1), so at least 16 of the 82 were opposition votes. adjudications.support: החוק נדון בכנסת בקריאה ראשונה ביום י' בתמוז התש"ן, 3 ביולי 1990, תחת השם "חוק למניעת מעילה באמון (נבחרי ציבור)"
adjudications.reason: Uriel Lin, chair of the Constitution, Law and Justice Committee, states the first-reading date when presenting the bill for second and third reading, and adds that two committees (House Committee and Constitution Committee) considered it after the first reading. First reading 3 July 1990, final vote 12 February 1991: 224 days, with no shortened committee stage. The gazette's bill date of 25 June 1990 that Coder B relied on is consistent with this.

adjudications.support: חבר הכנסת שפרש מסיעתו ולא התפטר מכהונתו סמוך לפרישתו, לא ייכלל, בבחירות לכנסת שלאחריה, ברשימת מועמדים שהגישה סיעה של הכנסת היוצאת
adjudications.reason: Values engaged: free and equal elections (principal subject, the anti-defection bar in new s. 6A) and rule of law (entrenched by the bans on office-for-vote agreements, s. 57A of the Elections Law and ss. 13A-13B of Basic Law: The Government). Section 6A withdraws the right to stand on any outgoing faction's list from a class of sitting members defined by their parliamentary conduct, and the 'consideration' qualification applies only to confidence votes, so a defection of conscience is caught too; that restricts the right to be elected and party list autonomy, a contradiction of free and equal elections. It is limited rather than sharp because it lasts one election, leaves candidacy on a new list open and exempts splits. Contradiction takes precedence over the integrity entrenchments, so I adopt Coder B's reading.

adjudications.support: הממשלה תניח על שלחן הכנסת את תכנית התקציב הרב-שנתית ביחד עם הצעת חוק התקציב
adjudications.reason: Value engaged: separation of powers only, as the principal subject, on the same reading as seq 19: new s. 3A(b) obliges the government to lay the multi-year budget plan before the Knesset with the budget bill, and s. 3A(c) binds the government's next budget to the plan it tabled, so the text adds to what the executive owes the legislature when the Knesset exercises its budget power. It constrains the executive, not the Knesset, and contradicts no value. Coder B's None would require the text to engage none of the five values, which a duty of the government toward the Knesset in the budget process does not satisfy; I adopt Coder A's reading.
